evidence: Types parsed with tomllib from the frozen bytes: gates/render 1 binary, gates/constraints 2 binary (both aggregation all_pass); scored/functional 42 binary (weights sum 58.5); scored/polish 6 binary; scored/visual 3 likert, each with points = 5. No binary criterion carries a points key and no type is outside binary|likert. FIT OF BINARY: every functional and polish criterion states an observable pass/fail behaviour and ends in an explicit 'Fails if ...' list (e.g. functional/judge.toml:29 'Fails if either join loses or duplicates a character ...'; polish/judge.toml:50 'both must be shown as unavailable (disabled)'; polish/judge.toml:68 'The page must not scroll sideways ... Fails if the page needs sideways scrolling'). The two binary criteria that look at appearance are discrete tests, not degree-of-quality: functional/judge.toml:173 'must show five visibly different treatments ... Fails if any two of those five categories look the same' and :182 the four-category HTML equivalent. I found no binary criterion asking for a degree of craft (no 'polished', 'clean', 'well designed' wording); the nearest, polish/judge.toml:32 'main controls have understandable visible names', is bounded by 'Fails if a main control has no readable name, or if any of the three actions ends with no visible textual feedback', and binary polish matches the frozen template's polish dimension. FIT OF LIKERT: the three craft judgements are likert with an anchor written for every level 5,4,3,2,1,0: visual/judge.toml:25-30 ('5: clear and comfortable throughout, numbers aligned, caret and selection easy to see.' ... '0: no editor is shown.'), :41-46 and :57-62. visual/prompt.md tells the judge 'Each criterion is scored from 0 to 5 using the anchors written in it. Those anchors take precedence over any generic 1 to 5 hint from the scoring tool' and reserves 0 for 'the thing being judged is not shown at all'. This is the shipped template format (template visual/judge.toml also uses type likert, points 5, anchors 5..0), and SKILL.md:65 says to flag binary craft criteria or likert blocks with missing anchors, not likert itself; neither is present. Adversarial attempts: (a) a broken app that passes - an app with default browser styling cannot hide in a binary, it lands on anchor 1 of cw_visual_component_finish ('largely unfinished or default browser styling throughout'); (b) a conforming alternative that fails - a canvas-drawn editor is explicitly admitted in the colouring binaries ('or a screenshot when the editor draws on a canvas'), and the visual prompt forbids penalising colour choice. Neither produced a type-fit defect. RUNTIME EVIDENCE (earlier candidate only, not these bytes): the hosted oracle run recorded cw_visual_editor_readability raw 5 value 1.0, cw_visual_workspace_layout raw 4 value 0.75, cw_visual_component_finish raw 5 value 1.0, visual 0.9167, so the likert type is accepted and graded by the configured judge. NOTE (template-inherited, not a task defect): raw 4 -> 0.75 shows the scorer normalises as (raw-1)/4, so anchors 1 and 0 are both worth nothing (how a raw 0 is treated, clamp or negative, is not measured in any available run). The sixth '0' anchor therefore adds no gradation; the task copies the template's 0..5 anchor shape exactly, so it is not for this task to change. The three anchors at levels 4/3 are terse ('one or two minor distractions', 'several crowded or uneven areas') but each level is described and distinguishable by count of flaws.
